### Internet outage and WAN failover (added 2026-09)

After the Emberline Metalworks outage on 2026-09-01 (see MTG-2026-09-03-POSTMORTEM-EMS), for any site-down call:

1. Work RB-NET-001 (Internet outage triage) first.
2. If the client has a secondary WAN, run RB-NET-004 (Firewall WAN failover check) **before** waiting on the ISP. Do not assume failover worked because the firewall shows the secondary interface "up".

passages.title: Internet outage triage
passages.text:
### 2. Run the WAN failover check (RB-NET-004)

2. **If the site has a backup WAN** (LTE or second ISP), go to **RB-NET-004** now and run its "Check current WAN state" steps, including the secondary WAN addressing check. Do this before anyone power-cycles anything.
   - Failed over and users working: the site is degraded, not down. Downgrade to **P2** with a note, handle the backup-link side effects listed in RB-NET-004 (public IP change, scan-to-email, VoIP re-registration), and continue below to get the primary fixed.
   - Backup WAN should have taken over but did not (dead, misaddressed after an ISP modem swap, or failing its health check): that is a Tier 3 problem on top of the outage. Page Tom Kessler and keep going with step 3 in parallel.
   - No backup WAN on the client page: continue to step 3.

## 2. Priority definitions

We assign priority based on business impact. When you call or write in, tell us how many people are affected and whether they can work. The technician who triages your ticket sets the priority and may adjust it as more is learned.

| Priority | Definition | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 Critical** | Business down, or most users unable to work. | Internet outage at the office; server down; email down company-wide; all phones down; ransomware warning on multiple computers |
| **P2 High** | Multiple users affected, or a key business function degraded; or a single VIP/executive fully blocked. | A department cannot reach a shared drive; the main office printer used for all invoicing is down; Wi-Fi down in one wing; the owner cannot log in at all |
| **P3 Normal** | A single user affected; a workaround may exist. | One user's Outlook keeps crashing; one laptop won't connect to the dock; a single user's OneDrive won't sync |
| **P4 Low** | Requests, questions, scheduled changes, and new user setups. | New employee setup; add someone to a shared mailbox; install approved software; "how do I" questions |

If you believe a ticket's priority is wrong, call the support line and ask for the Service Desk Manager, Priya Raman. We would much rather adjust a priority than have you wait.

---

passages.title: Post-Mortem - P1 Internet Outage at Emberline Metalworks (2026-09-01)
passages.text:
## 1. Summary

At about 5:35 AM CT on Tuesday 9/1, a road construction crew cut the fiber line serving Emberline's building. EMS has a secondary cable internet connection configured for automatic failover on their FortiGate firewall (asset LR-EMS-0007). **Failover did not work.** The secondary WAN link was physically up, but its gateway setting was wrong after the cable provider swapped the modem in late July, so the FortiGate health check on that link had been failing for about five weeks without anyone noticing.

The whole site was offline: shop floor terminals, the cloud ERP, Microsoft 365, and Yealink phones. First shift starts at 6:00 AM. Service was restored over the secondary link at **7:21 AM** after Tom corrected the configuration onsite. The fiber was repaired and the primary link came back at **12:04 PM**.

- **P1 response SLA (Professional, 30 minutes, 24x7): met.** First human response at 5:58 AM, 17 minutes after the ticket was created.
- **P1 resolution target (4 hours): met.** Service restored 1 hour 40 minutes after ticket creation.
- **SLA credit:** none owed.
- **Client impact:** roughly 80 minutes of lost production time on first shift; about 60 of EMS's 88 users were on site during the outage. Phones down until about 7:45 AM.

   Rates are on the current price sheet in Atlas Docs. Do not quote a number from memory; read it from the sheet.
5. **Get approval for billable work** before starting. The approver must be listed under Authorized Contacts in Harbor PSA. Record their name and the time of approval in the ticket.
6. **Work the issue** using the matching runbook. For P1s, update the client at least every 30 minutes.
7. **Hand off** anything not finished by 7:00 AM: leave a clear internal note and assign to the right board. Tell the 7:00 AM triage seat in the Service Desk channel.

## 5. Guest Wi-Fi: keep visitors off your business network

Most of our clients have a separate **guest Wi-Fi network**. It gives visitors, patients, and customers internet access without letting them see your computers, printers, or server.

Good habits:
- Give visitors the **guest** network, never your main business network.
- Change the guest password every so often (we can do this for you; just submit a ticket).
- Don't connect company laptops to the guest network. It won't reach your printers or shared files.

Don't have a guest network yet? If you have UniFi Wi-Fi managed by us, it's usually a quick change. Submit a ticket and we'll take care of it.

# RB-GEN-004 Ticket notes and closure standards

## Purpose / When to use

Every ticket, every time. These standards exist so that anyone can pick up a ticket cold, so the client sees what we did, so billing is accurate, and so business reviews have real data. Priya Raman audits a sample of closed tickets every week against this runbook.

## Prerequisites / access needed

- Harbor PSA technician login
- Familiarity with RB-GEN-001 (priorities) and the runbook catalog in Atlas Docs

## Note types in Harbor PSA

- **Internal note:** technician-only. Troubleshooting detail, credentials references (never the credential itself), escalation chatter.
- **Discussion (client-visible):** what the client sees in the portal and in emails. Plain language, no jargon dumps, no blame.
- **Resolution:** required at closure. Client-visible.

## Steps

### While working the ticket

1. **First note within the response SLA.** The first human response (call, voicemail, or personal reply) is logged as a Discussion note with the method used, for example "Called Jane at 9:12 AM, left voicemail, sent portal reply."
2. **Use the standard internal note format** for each work session:
   ```
   Symptom: what the user reports, in their words where useful
   Scope: who/what is affected (user, asset tag LR-XXX-####, site, # users)
   Steps taken: numbered, specific (commands run, settings changed, results)
   Result: fixed / partially fixed / not fixed
   Next step: what happens next and who owns it
   ```
3. **Be specific.** "Fixed printer" fails audit. "Stopped spooler, cleared C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS, started spooler, test page OK" passes.
4. **Never paste passwords, MFA codes, recovery keys, or Temporary Access Passes** into any note. Write "credential stored in LockBox Vault entry <name>" or "TAP issued by phone."
5. **Record identity verification** for any password, MFA, or access change: method and who confirmed (see RB-ACC-001 and RB-ACC-002).
6. **Record approvals** for anything billable or anything needing authorization (approver name, role, time).
7. **Keep runbook_ref accurate.** If you ended up using a different runbook than triage expected, update the field.
8. **Update the client** at the cadence for the priority: P1 every 30 minutes, P2 at least every 2 hours, P3 at least once per business day while active, P4 when status changes.

### Time entry

9. Enter time **against the ticket**, not at end of day from memory. Increments are 15 minutes for business-hours work.
10. Choose the correct **work type**: Remote, Onsite, After Hours, or Project. Work type drives billing and the Professional onsite bucket.
11. After-hours billable work has a 1-hour minimum; enter actual time and Harbor applies the minimum on the invoice.
12. If you believe the work is out of scope (not covered by the client's tier), mark the entry **Billable - Review**. The account manager reviews before invoicing. Do not argue billing with the user.

### Closure

13. **Confirm with the user** that the issue is resolved before closing. A call or a reply saying "it's working" is ideal.
14. If the user does not respond, use the **3-touch rule**: three contact attempts over at least 3 business days (for example, call + email on day 1, email on day 2, final email on day 3 stating the ticket will close). Then close with status **Closed - No Response**. The user can reply to reopen within 7 days.
15. **Write the Resolution note** (client-visible): one to three sentences, plain language. What was wrong, what we did, anything the user should do.
16. **Set the closure fields:** root cause category, runbook_ref, and whether a knowledge gap was found ("Runbook update needed" checkbox). Checking the box sends the ticket to the runbook owner listed in Atlas Docs.
17. **Do not close parent tickets** until all child tickets are resolved and the client has a summary.

## Priority guidance

- Do not change priority silently. If you change it, add an internal note with the reason.
- Closing a P1 requires a short internal summary: start time, resolution time, cause, and whether the 4-hour resolution target was met. Priya or Marcus reviews every P1 within 2 business days.

## Escalate if

- A user refuses to confirm closure but the issue is clearly fixed: Priya Raman.
- You find you have been entering time to the wrong ticket or client: tell Samuel Ortiz (billing) before month-end invoicing.
- A client complains about note quality or what they see in the portal: Priya Raman.

## Ticket notes example (passes audit)

> Symptom: User (front desk, Foxhaven Dental) reports printer "offline" in Windows. Scope: 1 user, LR-FHD-0217, other PCs print fine. Steps: 1) Pinged printer 10.20.1.45 OK, web UI loads. 2) Stopped Spooler, cleared spool folder (3 stuck jobs), started Spooler. 3) Test page printed. Result: fixed. Next step: none. Verified with user by phone 10:42 AM. runbook_ref RB-PRT-001.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2020-02-03 | Greg Halvorsen | Initial notes standard. |
| 2 | 2023-05-22 | Greg Halvorsen | Added 3-touch closure rule and work types. |
| 3 | 2025-09-15 | Priya Raman | Ownership to Priya Raman. Added standard note format, credential rule, runbook update checkbox, P1 closure summary. |

passages.title: Post-Mortem - P1 Internet Outage at Emberline Metalworks (2026-09-01)
passages.text:
## 1. Summary

At about 5:35 AM CT on Tuesday 9/1, a road construction crew cut the fiber line serving Emberline's building. EMS has a secondary cable internet connection configured for automatic failover on their FortiGate firewall (asset LR-EMS-0007). **Failover did not work.** The secondary WAN link was physically up, but its gateway setting was wrong after the cable provider swapped the modem in late July, so the FortiGate health check on that link had been failing for about five weeks without anyone noticing.

The whole site was offline: shop floor terminals, the cloud ERP, Microsoft 365, and Yealink phones. First shift starts at 6:00 AM. Service was restored over the secondary link at **7:21 AM** after Tom corrected the configuration onsite. The fiber was repaired and the primary link came back at **12:04 PM**.

- **P1 response SLA (Professional, 30 minutes, 24x7): met.** First human response at 5:58 AM, 17 minutes after the ticket was created.
- **P1 resolution target (4 hours): met.** Service restored 1 hour 40 minutes after ticket creation.
- **SLA credit:** none owed.
- **Client impact:** roughly 80 minutes of lost production time on first shift; about 60 of EMS's 88 users were on site during the outage. Phones down until about 7:45 AM.

passages.title: Post-Mortem - P1 Internet Outage at Emberline Metalworks (2026-09-01)
passages.text:
## 3. Root cause

1. **Direct cause:** The secondary WAN (wan2) had a static IP and gateway from the previous cable modem. After the cable provider replaced the modem (late July), wan2 could not route traffic. The link still showed "up".
2. **Why nobody noticed:** Beacon RMM monitored FortiGate WAN **interface link state** only (since REL-2603 in March). It did not monitor the SD-WAN health check. The FortiGate logged the wan2 health check failure starting **2026-07-28** but those logs were not alerting anywhere.
3. **Why the quarterly check did not catch it:** RB-NET-004 describes a quarterly failover check for every client with a secondary WAN. That check was not being done for most clients. Tom raised this at the 7/22 runbook review; it was parked for Q4.
4. **Why the client change was invisible to us:** EMS called the cable provider directly about a slow connection in July and the provider swapped the modem. There is no step in our client communications asking clients to tell us about ISP equipment changes.

- Mailboxes, shared folders, and Teams they need access to
- Whether they need a computer, phone, or printer setup
- A mobile phone number

With 3 business days, we can create the account, assign a license, prepare a computer, and make sure everything works on day one. If you need a new computer ordered, tell us as early as possible so shipping doesn't hold things up.

### Departing employees

Tell us as soon as you know. We disable the account, secure the mailbox, and collect a list of their equipment. Requests received before 3:00 PM on a business day are completed the same day. For sensitive departures, call us so we can act immediately.

---

passages.text:
## Notice requirement

- Clients must request new users **at least 5 business days before the start date.** This is in the 2026 service catalog and the client onboarding form.
- If a request arrives with less than 5 business days of notice: accept it, set P4, tell the requester we will do our best but cannot guarantee everything (especially hardware) will be ready, and flag the account manager (Alicia Brandt or Kevin Duong) in an internal note. Do not refuse the request.
- Hardware that must be ordered (Dell build-to-order) typically takes 5-10 business days. If the client wants a new laptop and gives short notice, offer a loaner from the client's spare pool if they have one (check their Atlas Docs page).
